description: Historical forecast definition: which archived forecast to return instead of history or live forecast. Used by solargis_public_TS_historical_forecast_request.schema.json.

HistoricalForecast.description: Which historical forecast to return. type CONCATENATED: fixed lead; for every day (D*) or time step (H*, M*) of fromDate..toDate, the forecast delivered a fixed number of days or delivery intervals before it, joined into one series, as an operational delivery would have received it; one series per requested lead period. type SINGLE: fixed issue; one snapshot, the forecast as available at processingDateTime, at most 5 days ahead.

type.description: CONCATENATED: one series built from forecasts with the same lead. SINGLE: one forecast as available at one instant.

leadPeriods.description: CONCATENATED only. Lead periods to return, all D* or all H* / M*. Every requested column that depends on the forecast irradiance (irradiance, its derived and PV columns, LEADTIME) is returned once per lead period, named <column>_<leadPeriod>, e.g. GHI_D1, PVOUT_H1, LEADTIME_D1, and carries the lead period in its column metadata (leadPeriod). The suffix is added for a single lead period too. Other columns (meteo, ALB, sun position) are the same for every lead period and are returned once, without suffix and without leadPeriod.
leadPeriods.$comment: Pick the family by how often the client receives a forecast (H* hourly, M15_* every 15 minutes, M30_* every 30 minutes) and the number in the name by how many intervals ahead it acts on it, so the series mirrors its real delivery. Same lead time, shorter interval = fresher data: M15_4 is not H1.

processingTime.description: CONCATENATED with D* lead periods only. Time of day the forecast is processed, shared by all lead periods, with an explicit offset (HH:MM+hh:mm, HH:MM-hh:mm or HH:MMZ), e.g. 10:30+01:00. Every day of the range gets the forecast as it would have been delivered at that instant: only forecast runs available by then are used (NWP runs a few hours after their issue time, satellite nowcast minutes after its time slot). Fixed offset, no daylight saving time.

processingDateTime.description: SINGLE only. When the forecast is processed, ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset, no fractions, e.g. 2026-03-03T10:30:00+01:00. Returns the forecast as it would have been delivered at that instant: only forecast runs available by then are used. fromDate must not be earlier than its date, and toDate at most 4 days after it.

sources.description: Forecast archives to read. NWP_FORECAST: numerical weather prediction models. NOWCAST: satellite-based nowcast. With both, they are blended as in operational forecasting. Default: every source that can contribute, as in the operational delivery - [NWP_FORECAST] when all leadPeriods are D1-D4, otherwise [NWP_FORECAST, NOWCAST]. NOWCAST covers only the first hours after the forecast is processed, so it is used for D0, H* and M* and never reaches D1-D4, also when D0 is requested next to them. NOWCAST alone is accepted for H* and M* only.

allOf.$comment: SINGLE: processingDateTime required, leadPeriods and processingTime forbidden.
H* and M*: processingTime forbidden, the lead alone defines the forecast.
D1-D4 without D0: no NOWCAST, its horizon of a few hours cannot reach the next day.
D0 and SINGLE: NOWCAST alone is rejected, a whole-day window always exceeds the nowcast horizon. Add NWP_FORECAST.

LeadPeriod.description: Lead period of a historical forecast. D0-D4: the forecast processed that many days before each target day (D0: the same day), at processingTime. Intraday lead periods name the delivery interval, then the number of intervals: H0-H4 hourly delivery, M15_0-M15_11 delivery every 15 minutes, M30_0-M30_5 delivery every 30 minutes. Each time step comes from the latest delivery made at least that many intervals before it, e.g. H1: 1 hour, M15_2: 30 minutes, M30_1: 30 minutes. With a 30-minute interval one delivery serves two 15-minute time steps, so M30_1 gives the time steps 30 and 45 minutes after its delivery. H* and M* blend satellite nowcast with NWP forecast.
